text:
sophie: Quick heads-up — I'm trying to bring Kerosene-7B into Dedicated. License file on modelhub says 'Non-commercial, no redistribution' but it's kinda vague about derived/quantized weights. If we quantize and ship qweights to a customer's dedicated pool (they have access to VM), is that redistribution or hosting? cc @liz-legal :thinking_face:

drew: short answer: depends on whether customer can extract the weights. If it's just serving inside a VM they don't download from, still fuzzy for some licenses. Also watch for attribution clauses — some require notice in product docs.

liz-legal: Hi — I skimmed the license. Two key clauses: (1) redistribution prohibition, (2) derivative works/transformations not explicitly permitted. Quantization may be considered a derivative by some licensors. If Dedicated means we transfer binary artifacts (weights) into customer-controlled VMs or give them a downloadable bundle, that's redistribution. If we host in a controlled environment where Redwood retains custody and the customer only gets API access, that's hosting.

aj: To add — we have precedent with Fennel and Marlin where the ask was to either (a) get a commercial sublicense from upstream, or (b) provide a hosted-only option in Dedicated (we run everything in customer VPC but keys/weights remain in our KMS/encrypted volume and we do not hand off weight files).

maria: From evals: Kerosene-7B int8 quant drop: +0.6 ppl, -0.8 wins on benchmarks but hallucination regressed on long-form summarization. We were planning to offer a pre-quantized package for faster cold-starts. If legal won't allow redistribution, we could instead do runtime quantization in-place (on startup) so we never store/export qweights.

tim: Implementation note — runtime quantization (we mmap fp16 weights and perform in-RAM quant step) is doable but increases first-request latency ~4–6s. Also we'd need a runtime flag to prevent any "export weights" operation across Dedicated images.

license-bot: link: https://redwood-internal/model-licenses/kerosene-7b.txt (automated scan: commercial_use=N, redistribution=PROHIBITED, derivative=UNCLEAR)

sophie: ok, sounds like two options:
- ask upstream for a commercial redistrib / sublicense (long lead)
- provide hosted-in-customer-VPC where weights are not downloadable and never leave our encrypted volumes
Which one is realistic for Sales? @aj any call on commercial path?

aj: Sales has a couple deals willing to sign on if we can get a clean commercial license. I'll flag legal to start outreach, but timeline 2–6 weeks. For short-term, prefer hosted-in-VPC custody model.

drew: for the custody model we need to lock down our packaging scripts. Pasting the dangerous CLI we must avoid in Dedicated: 
```
# DO NOT RUN IN DEDICATED WITHOUT APPROVAL
rdx pkg export-weights --model kerosene-7b --quant int8 --out /tmp/kerosene-q.bin
```
Instead we'll use the secure-rehost flow: 
```
rdx pkg secure-run --model kerosene-7b --quant runtime --no-export --kms-key=arn:... 
```

maria: also we should pin a benchmark set for pre/post quant gating. Proposed checks: MMLU subset, longform-summarize on 20 long docs, and 1k prompt latency distribution. If int8 causes >1.0% regression in any metric, block auto-release.

liz-legal: Agreed on gating. One more legal ask: include attribution text in customer onboarding and product TOS if we get permission. If upstream requires attribution we must capture a copy of the license in the console and in billing emails.

Tim: I'll add an env var REDWOOD_NO_EXPORT and a runtime assert to refuse any export call if running in Dedicated custody mode. Will also add audit log event when quantization runs.

sophie: OK next steps: (1) @aj start license outreach today, (2) @tim and @drew implement runtime-no-export + audit, (3) @maria and @drew add benchmark gating to CI, (4) @liz-legal draft required attribution text. I'll prep a short customer note for Sales. Thanks all :+1:

aj: noting for tracker — legal outreach ticket #LIC-8723 created.

license-bot: automated note: uploaded license snapshot to ticket LIC-8723.

maria: quick add — quant perf numbers attached in thread: baseline ppl 12.4 -> int8 13.0, longform rouge-L down 0.8 pts. Will attach full CSV in PR.

drew: cool. I'll make the PR with the no-export guard and CI gates.

sophie: closing loop — if anyone finds a slightly different upstream release with a permissive clause, ping thread and we'll re-evaluate.
